items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦贝宁传奇乐队Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与创作人Antoine Dougbé的合作录音，时间跨度为1977至1982年。Dougbé以拍手打出的Cavacha节奏为核心创作手法，该节奏源于鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车韵律中提取的律动，后蔓延至1970年代中期的刚果流行音乐。Dougbé身为伏都教实践者，以"魔鬼首相"之称闻名，其音乐融合伏都传统、古巴son、刚果伦巴与贝宁本土funk元素。评论指出，由于录音年代跨越七十年代末至八十年代初，制作音色已发生变化——吉他呈现塑料质感光泽，合成器开始出现，但音乐根基仍扎于七十年代传统。开篇曲目明显受古巴son影响，以合成器铺垫与高帽驱动的律动展开，吉他在中段开始多向推进。整体展示了一段虽短暂但浓烈的创作生涯，将西非传统节奏与拉丁美洲风格并置于同一框架内。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合 GuldGanger 的首张数字 EP，共收录五首作品，由北欧民谣领域知名歌手 Mia Guldhammer 领衔。乐队成员各自带来不同视角诠释传统曲目，整体弥漫着古旧、略带粗粝的氛围。开篇曲《Svennedal》以奔放的节奏展示主唱嗓音的说服力；《Nordgård》是唯一的原创作品，口簧与风笛推动出强烈的律动感；钦巴龙（Cimbalom）为传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》铺设精致背景；终曲《Ormsö》以器乐形式融合簧片、长笛与弦乐，呈现出不安分且令人兴奋的质感。作为数字发行的小厂牌作品，其传统根基与个体表达的平衡值得长期关注。

items.body: Anyankofo means friends in Fante, and the Danish seven-piece Total Hip Replacement have been collecting them in Ghana since a mini-tour there in 2013. In the winter of 2021 they formed a nine-piece band in Accra with Ghanaian highlife, reggae and gospel musicians and gave it that name, which also titles the album the group recorded at Kwame Yeboah‘s Kwashibu studio, released in 2022. A later trip to Ghana took them to Kumasi, the Ashanti capital and one of highlife’s strongholds, and a week of jamming there with players from Frafra gospel singer Florence Adooni‘s band and with Nsoroma of Accra highlife band Santrofi produced “The Search”. It is the latest single ahead of the album Ehum, and the band say it holds on to the improvised feel of the jams. The song is about hunting for purpose in a society that keeps speeding up, where the pressure to get ahead alone costs people their connection to each other. Singer and trombonist Victor West Hosbond fronts the band’s horn section, the signature of their sound, and on this single it rides a highlife rhythm. The band describe the mood they chased as “the hopeful spot between melancholy and euphoria“. They filmed the video over a couple of days at an old farmhouse in France during this summer’s tour, with Nell Le Corre behind the camera. Ehum, which the band translate as storm, comes out on 27 November with Ivorian reggae singer Tiken Jah Fakoly among the guests. A West African run through Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana opens the tour, then Danish dates follow from February into April, among them ALICE in Copenhagen on 26 February and Aarhus on 27 March. Stream “The Search” HERE and pre-order Ehum through THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Total Hip Replacement – The Search appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 丹麦七人乐队Total Hip Replacement与加纳音乐家在阿克拉组成九人编制，以Fante语"朋友"为名展开跨文化合作。乐队核心特征是铜管声部，融合加纳高life、雷鬼与福音音乐元素，在库马西与多支本地乐队即兴jam后完成这首单曲。歌曲主题关注现代社会加速带来的疏离感与对人生意义的追寻，乐手形容音乐状态为"忧郁与狂喜之间的希望地带"。编曲以高life律动为基底承载铜管旋律，保持即兴创作的鲜活感。新专辑邀请科特迪瓦雷鬼歌手Tiken Jah Fakoly参与，巡演横跨西非三国与丹麦多地。整体呈现欧洲爵士底色与西非传统音乐的对话，是一次有诚意的跨大陆融合实践。

items.body: Swedish duo Svaj. released a remix of the alan is waiting track “where you disappear” on 2 October 2026. The one-track single, titled “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild),” streams on Spotify and is available for download on Bandcamp and Subvert. The original song was written and sung by alan is waiting, the recording name of a Stockholm-based electronic artist whose debut album, “The Last of You,” came out in 2024. Svaj., the duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg based in Blackeberg, Stockholm, reworked the track for the remix. The release keeps alan is waiting’s original vocals. In a newsletter announcement, Svaj. described the result as “a wonky, New Order-tinged full-on synth-pop hit song.” where you disappear – Svaj. rebuild by Svaj., alan is waiting A visualizer for “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” is available on YouTube. About Svaj. Svaj. is the Stockholm duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg, based in the Blackeberg district of the city. The duo releases through its own TZW Produktion imprint. Svaj.’s Bandcamp profile describes its sound as “voice, electronics and bass. Minimal, experimental and industrial, yet melodic and danceable,” and compares it to Joy Division and Front 242. Svaj. issued its debut EP, “Rewind,” in March 2022. The songs reworked tracks originally recorded on tape in 1988, revisited with a Yamaha CS-10 synthesizer and a 1960s Tandberg reel-to-reel recorder. The duo’s second release, “Until We Fall,” followed in 2023. In 2024, Svaj. released the single “Cut Me Up,” a reworking of a song first written by Alien Waveform in 1989 and later issued as “Contagion” on the 1993 compilation “Tapping the Wires (A Selection of Futuristic Electro Mindbeats).” The digital single included a remix by UK industrial act Portion Control. The same year, Svaj. contributed “Brända Barn,” a reworking of a 1980 Swedish punk song, to the six-act compilation “SVÄRTA.” Svaj. released its third collection, “Maggots,” a six-track release, on 17 May 2025 through TZW Produktion on vinyl, CD and digital formats. The record includes a cover of John Cale’s 1974 track “Fear Is a Man’s Best Friend” and features contributions from Perra Wikström on contrabass and guitar and vocal effects from Devoid. Svaj. issued four music videos from “Maggots” through 2025, for “Experience,” “Fear,” “Portent” and, in October 2025, “Piglet.” The duo released the single “Patterns” on 19 February 2026. Svaj.’s catalog now runs from the 2022 “Rewind” EP through this month’s “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” remix.

items.body: Raveiac, a new rave-punk project from Turkey, released the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1” on SoundCloud on 2 October 2026. The five-track set gathers “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” tagged as techno on the platform. The compilation is part of a wider opening catalog. Raveiac released five tracks on 2 October: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It.” Two more, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit,” followed on 3 October, and “Backstall” closed the run on 4 October, for eight tracks in three days. There is no Bandcamp page yet. The catalog streams exclusively through Raveiac’s SoundCloud profile. Raveiac’s own description connects the project to “industrial rave, hard techno, breakbeat, EBM, gabber and digital hardcore,” through what it calls “a direct punk vocabulary: repeated commands, physical hooks and lyrics shaped by concrete rooms, surveillance, machinery, appetite and loss of control.” The project’s SoundCloud bio reads in full: “Rave-punk from Turkey. Dirty industrial raves, broken breaks, and digital decay. Repost what hits. Push it deeper underground.” ‘Rust & Strobe’ and ‘Swallow the Noise’ Raveiac singled out two tracks from the set for press attention. “Rust & Strobe” opens on metallic percussion and broken drums and closes on what the project calls “an acid-charged chorus.” “Swallow the Noise” is described as a faster industrial-rave track carried by a chanted vocal line and distorted production. Raveiac also presents a visual identity drawn from photocopied zines, neon imagery, torn paper, halftone noise and analog damage. About Raveiac Raveiac launched in October 2026 as an independent rave-punk project from Turkey. Between 2 and 4 October 2026, the project released eight tracks on SoundCloud: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It” on 2 October, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit” on 3 October, and “Backstall” on 4 October. Five of those tracks, “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” make up the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1”.

items._cn_summary: 为纪念作曲家史蒂夫·赖希九十岁生日，The Quietus发布了其"Strange Of…"系列的新篇章。撰稿人Sean Kitching提供了十个进入赖希作品的切入点，涵盖了从早期的磁带相位作品《It's Gonna Rain》、精简的《Clapping Music》到《Music for 18 Musicians》《Different Trains》等代表作。该文作为一份导览性介绍，引导听众探索赖希横跨数十年的创作脉络，涉及极简主义音乐、相位技法、磁带循环与扩展器乐编制等核心手法。作为资讯类内容，其价值在于为不熟悉赖希的读者梳理了一份兼顾早期实验与成熟时期作品的聆听路径，但因仅是节选摘录，未能展开具体的音乐分析与创作背景讨论。

items.body: Hermidgets, the anonymous Italian dark synthpop project, has released “Like Moths” alongside an official video. The single is out now through Bandcamp and is the fourth preview of Hermidgets’ third album, expected in early 2027. “Like Moths” was mixed by Matteo Sandri and mastered by Giovanni Versari. A bass-heavy opening gives way to rhythmic, buzzing synthesizers, with Hermidgets’ baritone vocal set against a danceable groove and a bright, wiry synth line that recurs through the track. The lyrics follow two people drawn into a relationship whose destructive pull has become part of its appeal, turning surrender into something close to devotional: “Learn how to pray for the pleasure of having nothing.” The video, directed around a concept developed independently of the song, was inspired by French artist Olivier de Sagazan. Shot in black and white, it isolates Hermidgets’ head and shoulders as white modeling clay obscures and distorts his features throughout the performance, with black pigment introduced later in the video. The project keeps its members unidentified, and the clay imagery extends that approach by withholding a clear view of the performer’s face. Like Moths by Hermidgets About Hermidgets Hermidgets is an Italian electronic project that does not identify its members, combining distorted synthpop and darkwave songwriting with self-produced visuals. The debut album, “The Mire,” was released in November 2020 and included the songs “This Is Over” and “Nothing’s Perfect.” The singles “A Flaw” and “Perks” followed in 2021, and “Meaninglessness” and “We Tend to Disappear” appeared on the mini-album “NIHIL” in June 2024, recorded with a limited setup of two analog synthesizers, drum samples and voice. Hermidgets began previewing a third album with the single “Fall Apart” in July 2025, followed by “Sundown” in December 2025 and “Could I Be Better” in March 2026, a song that revisits “Could Be Better” from the 2020 debut. “Like Moths,” released in September 2026, is the fourth single from that album cycle, with the full album expected in early 2027.
items._cn_summary: 意大利匿名暗潮电子项目Hermidgets发布新单曲《Like Moths》，是其第三张专辑的第四支预告单曲。曲目以厚重的贝斯开篇，随后引入带有蜂鸣质感的节奏化合成器，男中音人声与可舞动的律动相叠加，辅以明亮而尖锐的合成器线条贯穿全曲。歌词围绕一段被毁灭性引力所定义的情感关系展开，将屈服转化为某种近乎虔诚的仪式感。同步释出的官方MV由法国艺术家Olivier de Sagazan的创作理念启发，采用黑白拍摄，以白色雕塑黏土逐渐覆盖、遮掩演唱者面部，后段引入黑色颜料，强化了项目匿名性的视觉表达。整体制作由Matteo Sandri混音、Giovanni Versari母带处理，独立通过Bandcamp发行。

items.body: Susanne Jonsson and Jan Strandqvist of the Swedish band Red Mecca have returned after a hiatus. Their time away, however, was marked by intense and deeply painful experiences: Susanne’s sister was murdered and her relationship fell apart, while Jan struggled with addiction. Sometimes, nothing seems better than returning to creative expression—in their case, by making a new album. This record clearly holds great significance for them, even though the music remains true to Red Mecca’s signature sound and style. It is a polished album, balancing understated, sensitive, and refined tracks with a somewhat ‘harder’ Synth-Pop style. The songs are expertly crafted and beautifully sung by Susanne Jonsson, a vocalist who has nothing left to prove. Personally, I prefer their Electro-Pop style—which occasionally hints at EBM elements—as it really showcases their talent for creating great music. While some tracks may lack a definitive climax, I believe the choice to create a more restrained work was deliberate. This may not be my favorite album by the duo, but it stands as a significant and healing production in their career. (Rating:7½). Listen to “I’m On The Outside”: I’m On The Outside by Red Mecca About Red Mecca Red Mecca was set up by Jan Strandqvist, originally with vocalist Frida Madeleine, who left after four albums and was replaced by Susanne Jonsson. The Swedish duo released “Truth” in 2019, followed by the albums “Away” (2021) and “Stay” (2023), all on Massproduktion. Strandqvist discussed the band’s history, including a 2016 Swedish Manifest Award win and a soundtrack placement on “Killing Eve”, in a 2021 Side-Line Click Interview.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典二人组Red Mecca沉寂多年后回归新专辑，创作动机源自成员经历的家庭悲剧与个人困境。整张专辑在制作上保持了乐队一贯的风格路线，制作精良，作品在细腻克制与偏硬朗合成器流行之间取得平衡，旋律编排考究，Susanne Jonsson的演唱功力深厚。乐评者更偏爱乐队带有EBM元素的电子流行风格，认为这更能展现其音乐才华。部分曲目缺少明确的情绪高潮，但整体选择偏向内敛表达。专辑虽非二人最佳作品，却被视为具有疗愈意义的回归之作。Massproduktion厂牌为独立发行，文章来源Side-Line属于小众电子音乐媒体，文章长度充裕且为原创评论。综合来看，该专辑在暗潮/电子用户口味中处于中高匹配区间，但创新性与融合度评价较为克制。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items.body: Watch an exclusive premiere of the film of Ava Rasti’s The River, first performed as part of the 2025 Semibreve festival. The River by Iranian-born Berlin-based composer Ava Rasti was commissioned by Portuguese festival Semibreve and first presented on 25 October 2025 at the Capela Imaculada do Seminário Menor in Braga. The performance brought together Rasti and a string quartet composed of Filipa Abreu (violin), Vânia Oliveira (viola), Tiago Mendes (cello) and Catarina Coelho (cello). The work takes the Piave river in northern Italy as its inspiration, a landscape in which the present is intertwined with the traces of wars and violence from its past. Rasti constructs these fragmented memories, recontextualised and transformed into sounds. Wire subscribers can read Claire Sawer's review of Semibreve 2025 here.

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — Truly mind blowing album. Arguably one of the most manifold records from the dusk of that decade. HIGH TIDE have been one of the most important underground rock acts of that era. This album really blew my mind the first time I heard it. I almost did not believe that it released in 1969. Very few bands were so heavy back then. HIGH TIDE is so damn heavy, it really pisses me off that I can't recall a single magazine or online "list" of proto-metal bands that mentions these guys. You can find fragments of early doom in songs like "Futilist's lament" & "Missing out". You can hear neoclassical influences on the guitar riff on "Walking down their outlook". Also, on the same song, listen carefully the guitar lick on 2:20 (Judas Priest anyone?!?!?). And that violin... Majestic. Enchanting. Listen to "Pushed, but not forgotten". Amazing stuff, honestly. Some people may say that the [&*!#]ty production fits with the music and the atmosphere, I say it steals the music's grandeur.
items._cn_summary: High Tide 1969年专辑以小提琴与吉他为核心，开创性地将古典化旋律与沉重失真结合，预示了后来重金属的雏形。乐评指出其早期doom片段与新古典主义影响，如《Walking down their outlook》2:20处的吉他licks被比作Judas Priest前兆。小提琴在《Pushed, but not forgotten》等曲目中展现出庄严而迷人的张力。整体制作粗糙，乐评认为这反而削弱了音乐应有的宏伟感。作为地下前卫摇滚作品，其在小提琴驱动重型化方面的探索具有前瞻性，但制作层面与纯粹实验性前卫/先锋作品仍有距离，属于面向原型金属/早期前卫摇滚爱好者的重要历史文本。

items.body: English post-punk band Killing Joke released their self-titled debut album, “Killing Joke,” on 5 October 1980 through E.G. Records, distributed by Polydor Records. The record turns 46 this year. Killing Joke recorded the album in August 1980 at Marquee Studios in London and produced it themselves, with Phil Harding as engineer. Drummer Paul Ferguson described the sessions as recorded live with “no overdubs to speak of.” The eight-track UK LP runs: “Requiem” “Wardance” “Tomorrow’s World” “Bloodsport” “The Wait” “Complications” “S.O.36” “Primitive” The original US pressing added “Change,” the B-side of the “Requiem” single, between “Complications” and “S.O.36.” “Wardance” came out as a single in February 1980, ahead of the album, and “Requiem” followed as a single in September 1980. The album entered the UK Albums Chart on 25 October 1980 at number 41 and later peaked at number 39. Its cover collages a photograph by Don McCullin of CS gas clashes in Derry, Northern Ireland, in 1971, designed by Mike Coles. In 2019, Pitchfork placed the album at number 9 on its list of the 33 best industrial albums of all time. “The Wait” was covered by Metallica on the 1987 “Garage Days Re-Revisited” EP and later included on “Garage Inc.,” “Primitive” was covered by Helmet in 1993, and “Requiem” was covered by Foo Fighters in 1997 as a B-side to “Everlong.” About Killing Joke Killing Joke formed in October 1978 in Notting Hill, London. Jaz Coleman (vocals, keyboards) and Paul Ferguson (drums) met in late 1978 and placed an announcement in Melody Maker in February 1979 reading “Bass, lead, to tell the killing joke, we mean it man!” Guitarist Geordie Walker and bassist Martin “Youth” Glover answered and completed the original line-up. The band released its debut EP, “Turn to Red,” as a 10-inch on 26 October 1979 on Malicious Damage, the label Killing Joke ran with graphic artist Mike Coles. Recorded in August 1979 at Gooseberry Sound in London, the EP drew airplay from BBC Radio 1’s John Peel. The “Almost Red” EP followed that November, and the single “Nervous System,” with “Turn to Red” as its B-side, came out in December 1979. Killing Joke then signed to E.G. Records for the self-titled debut album, released on 5 October 1980. The band’s next albums were “What’s THIS For…!” (1981) and “Revelations” (1982), after which Youth left the band and was replaced by Paul Raven on bass. “Fire Dances” followed in 1983 and “Night Time” in 1985, the album that carried the single “Love Like Blood” and brought the band its widest chart exposure to date. Killing Joke continued recording and touring into the 2010s with albums including “Absolute Dissent” (2010), “MMXII” (2012) and “Pylon” (2015), with Jaz Coleman and Geordie Walker as the group’s only constant members. Geordie Walker died in November 2023 at the age of 64, as Side-Line reported at the time. The band’s 1980 debut album remains the record that introduced the Killing Joke sound now marking its 46th anniversary this October.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评以纪念性质梳理了英国后朋克乐队Killing Joke 1980年同名首张专辑的历史背景。内容涵盖录制细节（1980年8月在伦敦Marquee Studios录制，几乎无叠录）、曲目列表、唱片发行历史、封面设计来源（Don McCullin1971年德里冲突照片拼贴），以及Pitchfork将其列入工业音乐最佳专辑第九位的评价。文章还详述了乐队成员组建过程、厂牌沿革、早期EP发行，以及Metallica、Helmet、Foo Fighters等乐队对其中曲目的翻唱记录。整体属于信息性历史回顾，聚焦于唱片数据与背景资料，对专辑实际音乐风格、声响特征及艺术价值的深度分析较为有限。

items.body: Einstürzende Neubauten’s debut studio album, “Kollaps,” turns 45 this year. The German industrial band released the record on 5 October 1981 through the Hamburg label ZickZack. It remains the first official full-length release by Blixa Bargeld, N.U. Unruh and F.M. Einheit under the Einstürzende Neubauten name. “Kollaps” runs 38 minutes across eleven tracks, recorded in Berlin in 1981 and produced by the band itself. The album mixes rough punk-derived song structures with noise generated from self-built devices, electronics and metal plates and other found objects, a method that became the band’s signature. The tracklist includes “Tanz Debil,” “Steh auf Berlin,” “Negativ Nein,” “U-Haft Muzak,” “Draußen ist Feindlich,” “Schmerzen Hören (Hören mit Schmerzen),” “Jet’M” (a cover of Serge Gainsbourg’s “Je t’aime… moi non plus”), the title track “Kollaps,” “Sehnsucht,” “Vorm Krieg” and “Hirnsäge.” Later CD reissues appended additional tracks, including a live 1987 recording of “Negativ Nein.” Trouser Press described the record as “one of the most shocking visions ever committed to vinyl.” “Kollaps” is also listed in the reference book “1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.” The album has since been reissued, including a 2002 edition paired with the 1982 dub companion “Stahldubversions.” About Einstürzende Neubauten Einstürzende Neubauten formed in Berlin in 1980 around vocalist and guitarist Blixa Bargeld and percussionist N.U. Unruh. The band’s name translates to “collapsing new buildings,” a reference to construction failures in West Berlin at the time. From the outset, the group built its sound around self-made and adapted instruments, including power tools, scrap metal, oil drums and construction debris, played alongside conventional guitar, bass and vocals. F.M. Einheit joined on percussion before the band’s first LP. The band’s earliest recorded appearance came via the cassette-only “Stahlmusik” in 1980. Einstürzende Neubauten signed to the Hamburg independent label ZickZack, which released “Kollaps” on 5 October 1981, the band’s first official studio album. The record was recorded in Berlin during 1981 and produced by the band itself, with no outside producer credited. Following “Kollaps,” Einstürzende Neubauten continued to record for European independent labels through the 1980s, including “Zeichnungen des Patienten O.T.” (1983) and the compilation “Strategies Against Architecture ’80-’83,” before moving to Some Bizzare/Mute for later releases. Bargeld also worked as a guitarist with Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds from the band’s formation in 1983. Einstürzende Neubauten’s lineup has changed over four decades, with Alexander Hacke and Marc Chung both joining in the years following “Kollaps.” The band added bassist Josefine Lukschy in 2026, alongside confirmed festival dates and studio webcasts. Forty-five years after “Kollaps” introduced the band’s self-made-instrument method on record, Einstürzende Neubauten remains active, with the album standing as the starting point of that catalogue.

items.body: Toronto-based guitarist, Ayal Senior, developed an approach of listening, playing and collaborating deeply, unhurried and with space (hence the title ‘Yutori‘, which translates to ‘space’) after several creative sojourns to Japan. This philosophy of taking time and patience to create comes through the record’s immeansly laid-back and tranquil dream-folk vibes. The album grew out of of a hushed winter morning session in the recording studio with Senior and several of his friends and collaborators leaning into this almost zen-like method of playing and being in tune with each other. The music’s vast openness and meditative qualities reflect the nature of these sessions, giving them the loose and communal feeling of tight improvised jams. This cooperative energy gives the record a sense of excitement, as it gives the impression the songs can go into any direction at any time. So your ear and attention are hooked right away, and they remain held til the needle reaches the deadwax on Side B. Throughout the album, you are treated to unique variations of instrumental ambient folk that splinters into cosmic string music and astral Americana sounds, with spacey pedal steel, acoustic and fried electric guitar, pearly vibraphones and warm cello. Some tracks are like mini-baroque symphonies, while others lean more into the psychedelic, with dreamlike atmospheric passages and stream of consciousness-styled distorted soloing. The record has the ambiance of a Nick Drake LP, but paired with the looseness and cosmic expansiveness of a Matt Valentine or even a Popol Vuh album. This is especially true with the track that finishes out Side A, “Well of Seven.” Yutori is as serene as a day spent floating around in a still pond, as pastoral as a walk through a freshly snow-covered forest and as illusory and wistful as a half-remembered daydream. If you need a bucolic and peaceful listen to soundtrack your autumn, then this is the album you should reach for. Click here to get your copy on vinyl or digital today. -KH
items._genre: dream-folk / ambient / psychedelic folk / instrumental folk
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由多伦多吉他手Ayal Senior创作的概念专辑，灵感来自多次日本创作之旅所领悟的'余裕'（Yutori）哲学——留白、耐心与空间感。专辑诞生于一段安静的冬日录音过程，多位乐手以禅意般的状态进行松散而即兴的合作，呈现出深沉冥想的氛围。整体编曲以原声与失真电吉他、太空感的踏板钢棒琴、珍珠般的颤音琴和温暖的大提琴交织，部分曲目呈现出迷你巴洛克交响曲的形态，另一些则滑入迷幻氛围段落与意识流式失真独奏。评论将其与Nick Drake的忧郁民谣气质、Matt Valentine的宇宙开放感以及Popol Vuh的精神广阔性相类比。这张作品适合作为秋季静谧时光的配乐，在宁静的池塘与新雪覆盖的森林意象中漫游。

items.body: Out of all of the underrated bands I know, Boss Keloid have to be among the most underrated. They have many virtues I could sing but the main one is that they just sound like no one else. Their type of winding, dense, and uniquely harmonic stoner/progressive rock is just inimitable. And so, I live between Keloid to Keloid release, craving the very specific flavor that only they can provide. Happily, my latest fix is almost here and good lord is it glorious! Float & Aperture leaves behind a lot of the size and grandiosity of Family The Smiling Thrush and the density of Melted On the Inch in favor of a hard to pin down etherealness. "Pedestal", the second track which I am very pleased to premiere here, will do a better job at explaining what I mean than I can. Check it out below. Float & Aperture by Boss Keloid God, I just love this band. On "Pedestal" you get a taste of the leitmotif which runs through the entire album, some strangely (and pleasingly) sweet, high pitched vocals, and a whole lot of that sound palette that makes Boss Keloid who they are. Which is what exactly? It's that insidious lead guitar line, the fact that I could mean any of the three (at my count) lead guitar lines, the bubbling bass, the way the whole thing feels off-kilter, hazy, and psychedelic to such a unique degree. And finally, it's the excellent lyrics, here (like on the rest of the album) turned very introverted, musing on meaning, intent, self-knowledge, and failure.The entire release is this good. Like "Pedestal", it's angry at times. At others it's alluring, fantastical, strange, self-flagellating, self-aggrandizing, and a few dozens other emotions and perspectives besides. It's similar to previous Keloid releases but also different, uniquely its own thing just like all of their other albums. God I love this band. Please listen to this band! The full thing drops on October 23rd and you can, and should, pre-order it from the Bandcamp page above.
items._genre: stoner rock / progressive rock / heavy psych
items._cn_summary: Boss Keloid 的新专辑《Float & Aperture》相比前作减少了宏大编曲与密集程度，转向难以归类的空灵氛围。主打单曲《Pedestal》展示了贯穿全碟的主导动机，配以异常甜润的高音人声，吉他旋律线在三条不同走向间交织，贝斯声部暗涌翻腾，整体呈现失衡、朦胧而独特的迷幻质感。歌词部分转向内省，探讨意义、意图、自我认知与失败等主题。情绪上从愤怒到魅惑、从自我鞭笞到自我膨胀不断切换，既保有乐队的辨识度，又开拓出独立于前作的新方向。

items.body:
For XD:I, the show extends well beyond a three-minute song.

Made up of SWAN, BETTY, HAZÈ, and KANA, the four-member girl group combine K-pop vocals, rap, and choreography with DJing and electronic music. Their live format revolves around a continuous set, with members moving between the decks and the main stage as they build the crowd’s energy.

Represented by THE ARK Foundation, XD:I have been developing that approach through club and party performances in Seoul, including a 40-minute live set at Jangchung Gymnasium in August. Their recent festival bookings included EDC Korea’s circuitGROUNDS stage on 3 October, bringing the project into the electronic music festival circuit.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by XD:I (@way2_xdi)

K-pop listeners may already recognise SWAN as Shin Jiyoon, formerly of Weeekly. A songwriter and composer as well as a performer, she brings her idol experience into a role that now includes DJing and longer festival sets. Her artist profile also details solo work spanning lyric writing, composition, arrangement, choreography, and styling.

Alongside her at the decks is BETTY, whose background includes club appearances and a runner-up placing at the PLIT DJ Competition. She moves between DJing, rap, MCing, and dance, helping maintain momentum and respond to the audience throughout the set.

HAZÈ adds vocals, rap, and performance to the mix. Her profile describes a more restrained approach to expression, offering a different presence within the group. Youngest member KANA contributes vocals and dance, highlighted by her clear vocal tone and expressive delivery.

Those individual strengths feed into a flexible approach to performing. SWAN and BETTY handle DJing, while all four contribute across the show, with their roles changing according to the track and the flow of the set. Songs connect through electronic sections, choreography, and crowd interaction, giving the members room to develop a performance over a longer stretch of time.

“XD:I has been developed as a group that can connect DJing, vocals, rap, choreography, performance and direct audience interaction within one continuous set,” says Chanjae Park, CEO of THE ARK Foundation. “Each member has a different strength, and those different strengths come together to create the full XD:I live experience.”

For an introduction to their recorded music, there’s ‘SPRAY U’. Released on 5 August, the tech house-based single establishes the electronic direction underpinning the group’s live concept.

XD:I plan to take that format to more clubs and international festivals while continuing to release music as a K-pop group. Their ambition is to make the transitions between the decks, the microphone, and the choreography part of what fans come to see.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

items._cn_summary: XD:I是一个四人女子组合，将K-pop的唱跳、说唱与DJ打碟、Tech House电子乐融合在同一连续演出中。成员分工灵活：SWAN（前Weeekly成员申智润）与BETTY负责DJ台，其余时段四人交替进行演唱、说唱与舞蹈编排，通过电子段落衔接歌曲，强调与观众的持续互动。文中提及8月在奖忠体育馆完成40分钟演出、10月登陆EDC Korea电音节circuitGROUNDS舞台，代表作《SPRAY U》为Tech House单曲。该文为新组合介绍性新闻稿，侧重活动与成员背景描述，对音乐本身的声响特征、制作细节或艺术创新缺少深入评析。

items.body: Review by Agnenrecords — Echorec featured in Prog magazine 106 (February 2020) in an article titled 16 bands to watch this year, before their debut album The Island had even been released. Currently based in Bath, the trio easily deserve a place in that list because The Island is an incredibly mature offering. They even had the audacity to attempt, and successfully pull off a subtle interpretation of the end section of Pink Floyd's Echoes during the 17 minute long closing track The Lamb Returns ? Pink Floyd, listed as 'an artist we also like', being one of the leading exponents of the Binson Echorec analogue delay effect which provided the young band with their name. Made up of Julian Kirk (vocals, guitars and keyboards), Brad McGinty (bass, vocals) and Jake Aubrey (drums and percussion), there's no compromise in the quality or quantity of either lead instrument; Kirk is a genuine multi-instrumentalist who can play stately Gilmour-like guitar but also does an admirable impersonation of Tony Banks playing a fluid ARP solo on The Cinema Show. Despite being momentarily reminded of David Surkamp on Safe at Home (the epigrammatic opener The Water is a piano instrumental) I declined to look for comparisons with Kirk's vocal style because his voice simply seems to fit well with the music. McGinty and Aubrey are also both very capable musicians, meting out inventive rhythm patterns during staccato riffing or bubbling and bouncing along in the melodic sections - this is the essence of the music, it's primarily melodic, it's not derivative, it has plenty of changes and uses a broad palette to produce a nicely-balanced modern prog sound with classic touches.The Island is a concept album that relates the story of a teenage girl's journey of self-discovery. Raised on a lighthouse rock by a single mother who is reluctant to grant her any freedom, she flees to the Island in search of her father. The truth is finally revealed in the epic The Lamb Returns, that her nuclear family fell apart following the early death of her older brother. It's hard to believe that the story isn't personal ? it's well constructed with suitable imagery of yearning, hope, doubt and resolution ? and it's certainly a bold move on a debut release.It's not really a big issue because the entire work is thoroughly commendable, but I don't think the lyrics, which work fine as part of individual song structures and as an overarching narrative, fully rise to the challenge of telling such difficult themes.Stuck in the middle of a pandemic, a streaming-only release is not unreasonable, though getting noticed in a vast industry geared towards rewarding established acts and/or instant gratification isn't going to be easy for a new band with a debut album. In my opinion, the interest generated by exposure through Prog magazine should be maximised by investing in a physical product to be ready for the merchandise stand when gigs resume. I'm pretty sure that Echorec's music will be greeted favourably by the prog community.Three and a half stars
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由巴斯三人乐队创作，是一张概念专辑，讲述少女逃离灯塔孤岛寻找父亲的家庭破碎故事，主题涉及束缚、年华逝去与和解。音乐以流畅的吉他、键盘、贝斯与鼓为核心，器乐编写密度高，段落切换频繁，调性上带有古典新前卫摇滚的痕迹，尾声段落引用了平克·弗洛伊德《Echoes》的回声处理动机。制作采用流媒体发行，混音保留了器乐之间的呼吸空间，节奏组在激烈与柔美段落间提供支撑。歌词在叙事层面处理较为克制，未充分展开家庭创伤的沉重主题。整体呈现成熟完整，但在实验性与声音设计层面未做太多越界探索。

items.body: Review by Agnenrecords — I was given the opportunity to review Jordan Rudess' WIRED FOR MADNESS before I'd ever listened to a note played by Dream Theater and equally shocking, I always used to skip over articles about the band in magazines and books. One good thing is that I was able to approach this review, for the keyboard player's fifteenth solo outing, without any idea of what the music would be like, although it's obvious that I've harboured preconceptions about the band he's most associated with. Another thing on the plus side, I know that Rudess is admired by musician friends whose opinions I respect, one of which lent Rudess his Kurzweil K2600 keyboard for a couple of performances organised by the Italian Dreamers during a Rudess family holiday in Italy around the time of Feeding the Wheel. The K2600 still bears Rudess' autograph. The album cover design neatly encapsulates the story behind the title track, an individual who accedes to becoming partially computerised and as his human self is reduced, he undergoes a procedure to upgrade his mental and physical capabilities. As a result he becomes increasingly separated from the outside world with his computerised portion performing the majority of his routine functions, allowing his mind to travel freely between madness and spiritual enlightenment. In a nod to previous prog epics, the track is split into two parts with a total running time of over 34 minutes and maintains a high tempo throughout. Without any Dream Theater reference points I have struggled to draw comparisons but in terms of wild, creative conceptuality and sheer musical density it comes close to Patrick Moraz's Story of i. It could easily have been dreamt up in 1974 and serves as a tribute to the 70's progressive rock keyboard players who influenced Rudess, Rick Wakeman, Keith Emerson and Patrick Moraz included. Having never heard his playing before I had no idea how good Rudess was, with elegant rhapsodic piano, authentic Hammond organ tones, and sinuous synthesizer runs. The modern sounding keyboards remind me of Eddie Jobson's work on the debut UK album and, when the rhythm section gets into a modern-jazz mood, like Dave Stewart on National Health's swansong DS al coda. I'm not a huge fan of the lyrics but they serve the composition well and, delivered by Rudess himself (apart from guest female vocals from Marjana Semkina in the role of an angel, and Dream Theater frontman James LaBrie at the climactic end to part 2), they are well sung. The track is heavy at times but there are sufficient strong melodies and tonal variation, almost all played at a frantic pace, to keep the listener interested. It goes without saying that his guest musicians are all of the highest calibre. With Wired for Madness parts 1 and 2 taking up more than half of the album and close enough to being able to fill a single traditional LP on their own, the remaining tracks run the risk of acting as filler, though this isn't really the case. Off the Ground is a straightforward pleasant, mellow, reflective piece, a welcome respite from the onslaught that's just taken place, but Drop Twist once again picks up the pace following an early arcade game-like intro. It may not be prog as we know it but the short instrumental allows Rudess to show his chops. Perpetual Shrine could almost be Drop Twist part 2, but if anything it's busier and funkier. It wouldn't sound out of place if it was used as the theme music for an 80s TV detective series based somewhere in Florida... The one track that feels to me to be there to make up the numbers is Just Can't Win. I'm being unfair because I'm not a fan of the Blues, but it performs a similar function to ELP's Tiger in a Spotlight, a moment of relief from the technical bombast but still a little self-indulgent. Here Rudess utilises the guitar talents of Joe Bonamassa and incorporates a full brass section; as a blues-rock song it can't be denied that it pushes all the appropriate buttons. Just for Today is another reflective, slow-paced number but it includes sweeping cinematic strokes before it gives way to the jazzy Why I Dream where the vocal phrasing reminds me of Supersister or Jeff Berlin on Gradually Going Tornado. Wired for Madness showcases Rudess' excellent playing and I believe he's pulled off something spectacular with the 34 minute title-track, an excess to rival anything from the 70s. It wasn't nearly as heavy as I'd feared but covers the whole gamut of prog and prog-related styles, with melody, rather than riff taking the lead. Furthermore, the pacy compositions that bookend the recording makes it sound as though the whole writing, playing and recording was fun. Three and a half stars

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以概念化的叙事为核心，标题曲分为两部分，总时长超过34分钟，讲述人类逐步机械化后意识在疯狂与精神启蒙间游离的故事。键盘演奏兼具古典优雅与现代合成器语汇，引用七十年代前輩如瓦肯、埃默森与莫拉兹的影响，并融入现代爵士律动与棱角分明的节奏织体。器乐密度极高，旋律性强，客席乐手阵容扎实，女声与主唱分别承担天使与高潮段落的叙事功能。尽管主体宏大，其余曲目仍保持水准，未沦为填充物。整体而言，这是一部结构严谨、键盘主导的长篇概念作品，风格偏向经典前衛摇滚的当代延伸。

items.body: Darkmechanic released the album “Hypercontrol” on 2 October 2026 through the Slovak label Aliens Production. The eight-track record is the industrial electronic project’s second album and its first release for the label. Alexander Borsov, who records as Darkmechanic, wrote, produced and mastered all eight tracks. “Hypercontrol” comprises: The deceitful idol Puppet Gloomy lake Cau the night cult Hypercontrol Go all….F Resolving a controversy Halloween (Bonus track) Aliens Production describes the album as “a mechanical colossus of industrial energy and electronic flashes.” “Hypercontrol” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp. Aliens Production is a Slovak dark electronics label operating since 1997. Side-Line has previously covered Aliens Production releases by the Polish electro/EBM act Fractal, including “Antidote” in 2023 and “Hide in the light” in 2026, both on the same label. Hypercontrol by Darkmechanic About Darkmechanic Darkmechanic is the solo industrial electronic project of Alexander Borsov, who also records as Dark The Keeper and Stellar Dynamics. The project’s first recorded appearance was a track on the compilation “Dark Virus X-Mas”, released by Russian Dark Community in 2020. Darkmechanic’s debut album, “Ghost Reflection”, followed in 2021, also through Russian Dark Community. Between albums, Borsov contributed remixes to other artists’ releases: “Blood For Blood Remixes” (2023) on DSBP, “Monolith” (2023) by Reagent, “Mvrtyr” (2024) by G.G.F.H. and “Lost EP” (2025) by Synaptic Defect. Darkmechanic also appeared on the compilation “Cyclone Front: Movements and Currents” in 2025. “Hypercontrol”, released on 2 October 2026, is Darkmechanic’s second album and the project’s first release through Aliens Production, five years after “Ghost Reflection”.
items._cn_summary: Darkmechanic 是 Alexander Borsov 的单人工业电子项目，2026年10月通过斯洛伐克厂牌 Aliens Production 发行第二张专辑《Hypercontrol》。专辑共八首曲目，全部由作者独立完成创作、制作和母带处理。厂牌将其描述为一座充满工业能量与电子闪光机械巨像，仅以数字专辑形式在 Bandcamp 上发行。作为独立制作人的作品，Borsov 此前参与过多个地下电子项目的混音合作，积累了 DSBP、G.G.F.H. 等厂牌的关联网络。该专辑延续了俄罗斯暗电子社群的传统路径，从俄罗斯 Dark Community 到斯洛伐克的 Aliens Production，呈现出东欧地下暗潮工业场景的连续性。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是声音记录者Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述实录。录制地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家的前廊，正值特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队之日。参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，共二十五人，其中不少是临时被吸引加入的邻里居民。录音中夹杂着一些自由式说唱，但主体是真实的口述。一位失去两个儿子的老人在讲述过程中情绪崩溃，反复道歉，而她本无须致歉——社会才是应当道歉的一方。专辑没有任何添加的音乐，全部声音来自街头环境。收益将捐赠给以循证公共卫生方法遏制暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。这是一份直面城市暴力创伤的田野录音文献，兼具社会纪实与声音艺术的双重属性。

items.body: Colossloth released a video for “Encoded Divinity” on 3 October 2026, a track from the album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites.” The album came out 2 October 2026 on Cold Spring Records, the project’s sixth release for the label. The video was produced by HAONDOKU Productions. The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites by Colossloth Watch the video for ‘Encoded Divinity’ The video is available on YouTube: COLOSSLOTH – ‘Encoded Divinity’ Promo Video. “Encoded Divinity” opens the album and runs 5:08. ‘The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites’ tracklist The album was announced in September with its full tracklist: “Encoded Divinity” (5:08) “Calculate Your Revolution” (7:00) “Awaiting MENA” (9:04) “Undertow Atlas” (10:34) “Only Adrift” (8:00) Cold Spring describes the album as centered on Theta Noir, a collective built around worship of Mena, a fictional artificial intelligence deity. The label calls the record “an automaton chant of cybernetic worship.” The album is available on CD in a matt-laminate digipak (catalogue number CSR375CD) through Cold Spring’s webstore, and for download via Bandcamp. Colossloth played an album launch show at The Globe in Glossop on 3 October 2026, alongside T.A.G.C. (Adi Newton of Clock DVA), Satøri and Llyn Y Cwn. Further dates follow on 7 November at St Anne’s in Barnstaple with Satøri and A Waste of Damnation, and from 27 to 29 November at Sheffield General Cemetery’s In The Black Midwinter event with The Golden Age of Doing Nothing and Decommissioned Forests. About Colossloth Colossloth is the solo project of Leicester, UK musician Wooly Woolaston, active since 2008. Woolaston has described Colossloth as “a one man Experimental Electronic artist where there are no rules to recording or playing music,” with a sound that has moved from long guitar drones toward harsher electronics with sections of melody. Woolaston released Colossloth’s first album through Doom Structure in 2008, followed by releases on Doom Mantra Records in 2009 and Dark Meadow Recordings in 2011. He later signed to Cold Spring Records, releasing “Anchored By Lungs” (2014), “Outstretch Your Hand for the Impress of Truth” (2015), “Heathen Needles” (2017), “Plague Alone” (2020) and “Promethean Meat” (2022), the latter incorporating drum samples and harsher rhythmic elements. Colossloth also appeared on the label’s “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” compilation alongside Coil, Merzbow and Mz.412, among others. Colossloth’s fifth Cold Spring album, “The Harmony Knife,” followed on 28 February 2025, a concept record drawing on Ted Kaczynski’s “Industrial Society and Its Future” and its argument for the psychological necessity of struggle, known as “the power process.” “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites,” released 2 October 2026, is Colossloth’s sixth album for Cold Spring Records, now accompanied by a video for its opening track, “Encoded Divinity.”
items._cn_summary: 这是英国莱斯特音乐人Wooly Woolaston的第六张Cold Spring厂牌专辑，延续其从长篇吉他drone向更严酷电子音乐演变的轨迹。整张作品围绕虚构人工智能神祇Mena构建概念框架，厂牌将其描述为"自动化机械颂歌的网络崇拜"。从已有的曲目信息看，作品时长结构偏向长篇叙事，融合了鼓采样、旋律段落与粗砺电子声响。新闻稿性质的报道还追溯了Colossloth在Doom Structure、Doom Mantra、Dark Meadow等厂牌的发展历程以及近期多场现场演出计划，内容偏向信息发布而非深入乐评分析。

items.body: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail released the single “Vile Train” on 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The track is the first digital single from the band’s forthcoming full-length album “Infinite Fountain,” set for release on 6 November 2026 through the same French label. A video for “Vile Train” accompanies the single. Night Nail’s Brandon Robert wrote “Vile Train” after a visit to the ash-covered ruins of Pompeii, Italy, where a Roman fresco depicting an angel and a demon locked in embrace became the song’s starting point. The lyrics follow two dreamers from separate realities who meet at the edge of their daydreams, fall into an obsession, and become trapped in a psychological cage of their own making. Robert describes the result as a “sonic assault of dark and brutal truths about love sung in a twisted but beautiful way.” “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago and co-produced by Night Nail in Berlin, with additional vocals and guitar by VV & the Void, the darkwave project of Berlin musician Valentina Veil. Watch the video for ‘Vile Train’ The official video for “Vile Train” is available on YouTube: Night Nail – ‘Vile Train’ (Official Video). ‘Infinite Fountain’ due 6 November “Infinite Fountain” is available for presale on Bandcamp ahead of its 6 November 2026 release through Icy Cold Records. “Vile Train” streams on Spotify. Infinite Fountain by Night Nail About Night Nail Night Nail was founded in Los Angeles in 2013 by Brandon Robert and Justin Deaktiviere. Michael Carpenter Jr. on guitar, David Cluff on bass and Bryan Panzeri on drums joined for the project’s early releases. The project is now based in Berlin, Germany. An early self-titled EP drew press, college radio and blog coverage across the US, Europe, South America and Australia. The band’s debut album, “LA Demons,” was released in July 2018 on Cleopatra Records. Its title draws on Dostoevsky’s novel “Demons.” The sophomore album, “March to Autumn,” followed on 15 October 2020 through Cold Transmission Music. Pete Burns of Kill Shelter co-produced, mixed and mastered the record. Touring and session musicians Valentina Veil, Ilja Gavrilenko and Manuel Wagner contributed additional parts. In September 2023, Night Nail released the single “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher,” the first taste of the album “Fates Explained” on Metropolis Records. The single reached the top five of the Deutsche Alternative Charts. The “Fates Explained” video single followed that November. In January 2024, the band released a video for “Cracks In My Heart,” with Luna De La Torre on vocals, and in July 2024 issued “Early Demons & Demos,” a 10th-anniversary edition of early material. “Vile Train,” released 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records, is the first single from “Infinite Fountain,” due 6 November 2026.
items._cn_summary: Night Nail 是一支驻柏林的双人暗潮项目，由 Brandon Robert 与 Justin Deaktiviere 于2013年在美国洛杉矶创立，目前活跃于欧洲地下场景。新单曲《Vile Train》取材于庞贝废墟中一幅描绘天使与恶魔相拥的罗马壁画，歌词围绕两个来自不同现实的梦境者相遇后陷入执念的心理囚笼展开。制作层面，由 Chicago 的 William Faith 在 13 Studio 负责混音与后期，柏林乐队成员共同制作，并邀请 VV & the Void 的 Valentina Veil 贡献人声与吉他。厂牌 Icy Cold Records 为法国独立厂牌，文章信息量充分，但内容偏向新闻通稿而非深度乐评，缺乏对声音设计与音乐语言的实质分析，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、即兴方向距离明显，整体属常规暗潮文本。

items.body: M[SSΛNGR, the synthwave and darkwave project of Waukegan, Illinois musician Angelo Ochoa, released the single “Cycle” on 25 September 2026 through the label Anti-Joy. The track pairs synthwave and darkwave production with a modern pop song structure. Ochoa describes the results as “cinematic anthems.” “Cycle” was added to the Spotify curator playlist “Synthchronization: Sparkling Synths Take Over” following its release. The single streams on Spotify and is available across Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music, Tidal and SoundCloud. Ochoa states that no AI is involved in the production of his music. “Cycle” is the first single from Ochoa’s planned 15-track project “Evolution,” currently in production. Teaser clips for the project are scheduled to roll out through autumn 2026. About M[SSΛNGR M[SSΛNGR is the recording name of Angelo Ochoa, a musician based in Waukegan, Illinois, near Chicago. Ochoa writes and produces alone, combining synthwave and darkwave influences with pop song structures. “Cycle,” released through Anti-Joy on 25 September 2026, is the project’s first released single and the opening piece of the planned 15-track project “Evolution.”

items.body: Analogical Force has long occupied the productive tension between experimentation and the dancefloor’s accumulated memory. Hidden Soul sits firmly within that tension, fluent in its established language and meticulously composed. But perhaps the most exciting possibility lies just beyond that fluency: not abandoning the listener, but trusting them enough to take the familiar somewhere unfamiliar. Muscle memory and accumulated emotional shorthand [AF069] Hidden Soul EP by The 89th Passenger   The 89th Passenger returns to the release schedule of one of contemporary dance music’s more compelling production houses with Hidden Soul, from Paris-based Jeremy Cohen delivering five tidy, DJ-friendly excursions into the familiar architecture of breaks, pads, subs and euphorically melancholic atmospheres. This is music that understands the dancefloor not as a problem requiring reinvention, but as an existing language, complete with its own grammar, muscle memory and accumulated emotional shorthand. “Paper Wings” establishes that grammar almost immediately. Chopped breaks, rounded subs, 303 squiggles and luminous pads are looped into clean, recognisable frames, each element occupying its expected orbit. There is something almost architectural about the neatness of it: familiar components assembled into a functioning environment designed to communicate quickly, cleanly and without obstruction. “Hidden Soul” pushes further into the low end, drawing on break patterns whose familiarity is part of their appeal. Its immediacy is hard to resist; the rhythmic language seems already lodged somewhere in the listener’s body. “What it Takes to Fly” lightens the palette considerably, pairing pretty 303 work with gorgeous tones and gently arpeggiating synths. Its carefully managed peaks, troughs and breakdowns possess an almost cinematic emotional shorthand—the kind of musical optimism that could soundtrack an airplane disappearing into a sunrise. Music interested in making the familiar feel good :: “Eren” continues along those coordinates, allowing textures to breathe while the rhythmic components settle into a quiet, efficient momentum. It feels less like a departure than another room in the same building: different light, familiar construction. “Analog Serenade” finally shifts the pace and texture again, suggesting another route through the material without substantially redrawing its map. And this is where the record becomes more interesting as an artefact of contemporary dance music. Its boundaries are visible. This is not music attempting to make the familiar unstable; it is music interested in making the familiar feel good. The breaks remain breaks, the 303 remains gloriously 303, and the emotional trajectory arrives largely where expectation has already placed it. There is safety here, but it is designed safety: a deliberate perimeter around the possibility of surprise. Yet accessibility and predictability are not the same thing. Music can push its own materials beyond their comfort zone without alienating the listener. In fact, some of the most generous dance music does precisely this, inviting you into a recognisable room before quietly moving the walls. Safety can be useful, but it can also become lazy—an easy creative cheat in which recognition performs the emotional labour that invention might otherwise have to do. Analogical Force has long occupied the productive tension between experimentation and the dancefloor’s accumulated memory. Hidden Soul sits firmly within that tension, fluent in its established language and meticulously composed. But perhaps the most exciting possibility lies just beyond that fluency: not abandoning the listener, but trusting them enough to take the familiar somewhere unfamiliar. Hidden Soul is available on Analogical Force. [Bandcamp] [AF069] Hidden Soul EP by The 89th PassengerThe post The 89th Passenger :: Hidden Soul EP (Analogical Force) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: The 89th Passenger 的《Hidden Soul EP》由巴黎制作人 Jeremy Cohen 发行于 Analogical Force 厂牌，共收录五首作品。整张唱片以碎拍、低频 sub-bass、303 酸线合成器和旋律化 pad 构建出熟悉的俱乐部语法，每首曲目都在这一框架内进行微调而非突破。开场曲《Paper Wings》将 chopped breaks 与圆润低频交织，《Hidden Soul》进一步下探低频律动，《What it Takes to Fly》则以明亮的 303 与琶音合成器呈现近似电影配乐般的情绪起伏。《Eren》和《Analog Serenade》延续同质化的质感变化。乐评指出这张作品有意将熟悉元素打磨得令人舒适，边界可见、惊喜有限，但这种'刻意设计的安全感'正是它作为当代舞曲制品的趣味所在。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Finnish band Von Hertzen Brothers released their fifth studio album 'Nine Lives' in 2013 throughUniversal, having previously caught the attention of the press with the records 'Love Remains theSame' and 'Stars Aligned'. This quintet plays an interesting crossover of pop, prog, and folk,offering an eclectic yet accessible type of rock music that definitely has commercial potential butdoes not shy away from unconventional arrangements. The album 'Nine Lives' in particular issubjected to a high-energy, buzzing start, in the face of melodic numbers like 'Insomniac' and'Flowers and Rust', while its ending resorts to mellower, more atmospheric tones that are exploredon the longer songs 'World Without' and 'Prospect for Escape'. Certain instrumental sections are waytoo loud in the recording, especially in the faster tracks in the beginning, but I think thisproblem is taken care of in the second half of the recording. The vocals are fine, but some of thelyrics feel corny, while the album itself strikes you as almost too eclectic, which is probably whatVHB had wanted to do, but this aspect of it may disengage some listeners. I think the main issuewith 'Nine Lives' is the fact that there are very few highlights present. The record is quite solidoverall and the variety of styles covered provides for an engaging listen, but the songs featured onit are mostly hit or miss.
items._genre: crossover prog / pop rock / folk rock
items._cn_summary: 芬兰乐队Von Hertzen Brothers的第五张录音室专辑，以高能量的方式开场，收录了如《Insomniac》和《Flowers and Rust》等旋律性曲目，结尾则转向更舒缓、更具氛围感的风格，长曲《World Without》和《Prospect for Escape》是这种探索的代表。专辑融合流行、前卫和民谣元素，试图在可听性与非常规编曲之间寻找平衡，但整体呈现出过于折衷的倾向，可能让部分听众感到脱节。前半部分某些器乐段落混音过响的问题在后半部分有所改善。人声表现尚可，但部分歌词显得陈腐。专辑整体扎实但缺乏突出的亮点，歌曲质量参差不齐。

items.body: Mass Minor, the Austin, Texas-based darkwave and electronic rock project of Andrew J. Martin Jr., released the single “Get Up” on 2 October 2026 via Metropolis Records. Get Up by Mass Minor “This song is a conversation with God at 169 BPM about sin, money, mortality and the things we sacrifice our lives to,” Martin says of the track. “It comes from this idea of asking God to save us from problems we created ourselves. Maybe it’s not God’s job to save us. Maybe we need to fix our own shit. You’re the one holding the light. Get up.” A music video for “Get Up”, directed by Teresa Jolie and edited by Beau Loy, accompanies the release. “Get Up” follows “Nowhere Now”, issued as a single in late July. Both songs are set to appear on a new Mass Minor album, “Beyond The Edge Of Reason”, due out in late February 2027 on Metropolis Records. About Mass Minor Mass Minor is the Austin, Texas-based project of Andrew J. Martin Jr., who blends atmospheric synths and driving guitars with post-punk, synth-pop and alternative rock influences. Martin self-released the project’s debut album, “Become Each Other”, in 2020, followed by a run of singles later collected on EPs. The project built a presence in the dark alternative scene through radio support, multiple SXSW appearances and shows alongside acts including Twin Tribes, Ultra Sunn, TRAITRS, Vision Video, Urban Heat and Sacred Skin. Mass Minor signed to Metropolis Records and released the single “Nowhere Now” in July 2026, followed by “Get Up” on 2 October 2026. Both tracks lead into the project’s next album, “Beyond The Edge Of Reason”, due in late February 2027.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Metropolis Records旗下艺人Mass Minor新单曲发布的新闻稿式报道。Mass Minor是Andrew J. Martin Jr.的个人项目，融合氛围合成器与强劲吉他riff，跨越暗潮、后朋克、合成器流行与另类摇滚。"Get Up"以169 BPM的节奏构建了一段与上帝的对话，探讨罪、金钱、死亡及自我牺牲的主题，核心概念是向神求助解决自身制造的问题——暗示救赎需来自内部而非外部。歌曲由Teresa Jolie执导音乐录影带，延续七月发行的"Nowhere Now"，均为2027年二月专辑"Beyond The Edge Of Reason"的先行单曲。项目通过SXSW演出及与Twin Tribes、Ultra Sunn、TRAITRS等暗潮同台的现场经历积累声誉。整体内容偏厂牌宣传，缺乏对音乐细节与制作手法的深入分析。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
