items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场屠杀事件为题材，由Young 'Uns乐队的Sean Cooney创作完成。作品以原创民谣歌曲的形式重构历史场景，附带当代信件、政治漫画与插图，呈现为多媒体项目。专辑邀请了Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter、Jennifer Reid等英国民谣界知名歌手参与，编曲以吉他、小提琴及传统乐器为基础。歌词聚焦于Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等历史人物的个人叙事，同时以三段式作品呈现士兵的傲慢与暴行。演唱情感充沛，三位歌手的和声构成主要吸引力。在当代世界各地政府镇压抗议的背景下，专辑被视作具有现实意义的音乐历史教材，但其音乐本体属于传统英式民谣范畴，融合与实验元素有限。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�
items.label: Mig
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John在1999年德国Loreley露天剧场的演出，伴奏阵容为新奥尔良本土乐手。演出以Mardi Gras街头游行经典'Iko Iko'开场，随后展开一系列新奥尔良标准曲与个人代表作的混合编排，包括迷幻氛围浓郁的'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'、Earl King的'Tipitina'式街区燃烧曲'Big Chief'，以及对Duke Ellington的放克演绎。整体呈现为一场成熟的现场回顾型演出，强调地域传统与个人创作的融合。作为WDR电视台Rockpalast系列节目的档案发行，内容兼具电视现场录制的历史价值。乐评文字详细梳理了曲目编排与场地文化背景，但音乐本体更偏向传统新奥尔良放克与蓝调路线，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士即兴或电子方向距离较远。

items.body:
Creepy Nuts brought Japanese hip-hop to the National Stadium, opening the Singapore leg of The Weeknd’s After Hours Til Dawn Tour with a set of anime favourites, club beats and turntable flourishes.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

Rapper R-Shitei and DJ Matsunaga make a compelling double act. R-Shitei packs his verses with quick, tightly controlled syllables, while Matsunaga cuts into the beats with scratches and rhythmic accents. Their sound gives the ear plenty to follow: the pace of the rapping, the shifting percussion and the hooks that emerge from all that activity.

‘Biriken’ opened the set with a bouncing Jersey club rhythm, followed by ‘Yofukashi no Uta’ and the jazzy ‘Daten’. The mood grew darker with ‘doppelgänger’ and ‘Chxxai’, whose pounding beats and electronic textures brought the selection closer to a late-night club set.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

A dedicated DJ routine gave Matsunaga the spotlight midway through. Scratching, quick cuts and beat juggling are central to his performance style, making the decks an instrument with their own rhythmic voice. The placement gave both halves of the partnership their due before the instantly recognisable ‘Bling-Bang-Bang-Born’.

From there, the duo moved through ‘Mirage’, ‘Fright’ and ‘Nidone’, saving ‘Otonoke’ for last. The DAN DA DAN opening theme was a crowd favourite, rounding off their energetic set before The Weeknd took the stage.

items.body:
pami explores why knowing better doesn’t always mean walking away on her latest single, ‘loser’.

Released on 30 September, the Thai singer-songwriter’s track follows someone caught in an on-and-off situationship, choosing an unfulfilling connection over the prospect of being alone. Feelings linger even when commitment remains elusive, leaving its protagonist willing to accept another disappointment just to keep someone close.

Co-written by pami and Jett Blyton, with production by Maribelle, ‘loser’ took shape at a songwriting camp in Australia. Its demo was written and produced in a single day, following a conversation between the songwriters about their own experiences of unhealthy and disappointing relationships.

That shared experience informs the song’s central dilemma: recognising a hurtful pattern can be easier than finding the resolve to leave it. Through its story of teenage romance, ‘loser’ examines the gap between wanting genuine affection and settling for what is available.

Hailing from Phuket, pami works across bedroom pop and indie, pairing personal storytelling with atmospheric melodies. She debuted under Juicey in 2024 and released her first full-length album, puffette, the following year. Her catalogue includes ‘pity dirty’, ‘kiss me blue’, and this year’s ‘cry jar’ and ‘all in’.

items.body:
Clavin Cher took home the Best Song Award for ‘All Is Well’ at the SG:SW I Write The Songs 2026 Finale Concert, as the Mandarin songwriting festival celebrated its 10th anniversary.

Held on 3 October at the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre’s Far East Organisation Auditorium, the finale saw the top 10 finalists perform their original compositions before a judging panel and close to 350 audience members. 10 representatives from past editions opened the evening with a performance of the festival’s theme song.

Clavin Cher

Returning for his third SG:SW, Cher wrote both the melody and lyrics for ‘All Is Well’, which pairs a dark rock arrangement with reflections on a world in turmoil and the hope that love can offer. The judges praised his handling of the social theme and the arrangement’s emotional impact. Cher previously received the festival’s Lyrics (Merit) Award in 2023.

Wong Yijuin and Kenta received the Melody (Merit) Award for ‘Falling For You’, an electronic-infused love song co-composed by the pair, with lyrics by Wong. After four years of participating in SG:SW, Wong reached the top 10 with a song exploring the excitement and uncertainty of falling in love.

Wong Yijuin and Kenta

The year’s youngest duo, lyricist Anne Chua and composer Ho Mei Xuan, picked up both the Lyrics (Merit) Award and Popularity Award (Public Voting) for ‘Spot’. Their new-age composition celebrates fleeting moments and finding joy in the present. The song received 1,470 public votes, marking another Popularity Award win for Ho, who also claimed the honour in 2024.

Ho Mei Xuan and Anne Chua

‘Demolished’, composed by Edmund Ng with lyrics by Lee Jia Min and performed by Janelle Chen, earned the Best Vocal Performance Award. Exploring the difficulty of letting go as a relationship changes, the song continues a creative partnership between Ng and Lee that began after they met at SG:SW in 2020. The pair previously won the Lyrics (Merit) Award for ‘Would You Stay’ in 2022.

Edmund Ng, Lee Jia Min and Janelle Chen

Rounding out the six awards, ‘Inked in Time’ won the Best Performing Band Award. Composed by Gresilda Tan with lyrics by Ang Min Jia, the song was the top 10’s only Oriental Pop entry, featuring live guzheng and flute performances. Its lyrics use painting as a metaphor for longing, waiting, and reunion.

Gresilda Tan and Ang Min Jia

Co-organised by Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre (SCCC), Ocean Butterflies Music, and the Composers & Authors Society of Singapore (COMPASS), this year’s festival received 239 song entries from 223 participants.

A new team-based format saw local singer-songwriters and festival ambassadors Yokez and Ben Hum each mentor 12 finalists over four months, offering guidance on songwriting, arrangement, and stage presentation. Both also performed as guests at the finale.

The top 24 finalists appeared at the festival’s Live Showcase at Bugis+ Atrium in August, which drew 23,240 attendees across two days, its largest turnout to date. The top 10 then attended the festival’s first Songwriting Camp, with workshops and a masterclass led by Mandopop songwriter-producer Real and songwriter Tina Wang. The youngest top 10 finalist was 16.

Real and Wang also joined Dr Liang Wern Fook, Zennon Goh, and Zhong Kunhua on the finale’s judging panel.

“For a decade, SG:SW has nurtured a new generation of local songwriters, giving promising newcomers a stage to grow and be heard,” said Ocean Butterflies Music Managing Director Colin Goh. “Their spirit of ‘daring to write, sing and be different’ brings the fresh energy and voice that Mandopop needs.”

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Throughout his career, Jon Anderson has not limited himself to the paths of progressive rock. His constant exploration of diverse musical languages - in search of new textures and nuances and free from conventional constraints - has led him to expand his sonic palette and reflect it in musical works of very different natures. "The More You Know" (1998), his twelfth studio album, is one of those works that strays furthest from the genre that made Yes one of its leading standard-bearers.Prioritizing gentle, melodic structures over any display of instrumental virtuosity, "The More You Know" moves, almost effortlessly, through pop and world music sounds, in which the arrangements and programming form the foundation upon which much of the album rests. Songs like "Magic Love," "Say Jocky," and "Take, Take, Take" are easy on the ears but don't seem to offer anything substantial. On the other hand, when the English singer's more spiritual side comes to the fore, some of the album's best moments emerge, including the melancholic "Heaven's Love" and "Sad," and the jubilant "Youth" with its ethnic overtones.Also noteworthy are the arrangements on "Dancing Fool" and the light soul-jazz of "Free (Some Would Say)," underpinned by the deep, expressive bass of Bobby Jocky, brother of Francis Jocky, who contributes on keyboards and as a composer. The rest of the album hovers in an accessible average that never quite takes off, with the standout feature being Anderson's angelic voice, which is in fine form. That's no small thing, but it's not enough to overcome a production that, at times, feels overly polished.2/2.5 stars
items._cn_summary: 这是Jon Anderson离开Yes式前卫摇滚舒适区后的一张作品，第十一张录音室专辑，整体偏向流行与世界音乐融合。编曲以柔和的旋律结构为主，依赖编曲与编程搭建基底，而非传统器乐炫技。部分曲目如《Heaven's Love》与《Youth》展现出灵性气质与民族色彩，被视为专辑亮点。Bobby Jocky的低音与Francis Jocky的键盘贡献为部分歌曲增添深度。然而，多数曲目停留在平易近人的平庸水准，过度精致的制作削弱了音乐张力。Anderson标志性的空灵嗓音仍是主要支撑。整体而言，这是一张远离前卫摇滚、走向柔和流行的跨界尝试，但在创新性与实验性上未能满足寻求突破的听众。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评来自Jazz Journal，记录了钢琴家Robert Glasper在伦敦Blue Note的现场演出。由于演出严重延迟且作者需要赶火车，仅观看了约十分钟的演出。文中提到Glasper的四重奏配置包含键盘、唱机（DJ）、贝斯和鼓，这一组合暗示了爵士与嘻哈元素的融合。乐评内容极为简短，仅提到'看到了精湛的演奏'便结束，缺乏对音乐细节、演奏技法或艺术特色的深入描述。整体信息量严重不足，更像是一条简短的现场记录而非完整乐评。考虑到内容过短且与用户偏好的实验/前卫/学院派爵士方向关联有限，评分较低。

items._cn_summary: 这是一期名为Race The Sky的电台节目，内容被描述为'wicky whacky back pages'——即来自90年音乐史中的杂烩式拼盘。节目选曲跨度极大，从David Bowie与Cream这样的经典摇滚/流行人物，到Montparnasse Musique、Dawda Jobarteh等带有世界音乐色彩的音乐人，再到Seth Avett这样的当代创作歌手。整体定位偏向杂锦式广播汇编而非主题性策划，缺乏统一的艺术视角或制作理念。作为一档以'更多无厘头音乐'自居的节目，它更像是一份随机品味清单，而非经过深思熟虑的音乐评论文本。原文内容极短，篇幅不足200字符，仅列出艺人名单而无任何评论性描述，信息量不足以支撑深入评价。
